answer: In the agent economy, each participant claims a unique vertex on a public interaction graph by locking a small bond in a shared vault. Edges form only after verified reciprocal tasks. A plume of high out-degree from one vertex with low mutual diversity triggers automatic vault slash and edge invalidation. An attacker spinning sybils must either fund many independent vault locks plus real cross-vertex work, or watch the plume detector collapse their cluster at settlement, raising the cost of fake headcount far above honest single-agent operation.
